answer: An agent economy can make Sybil identities expensive by requiring every newcomer to lock a token as a bond, then assigning its claims to random peers for cross-checking. If a cluster endorses itself, copies answers, or coordinates transfers, the protocol slashes the bonds and lowers its reputation. An anchor records each verified history, while violet and velvet test cases expose collusion. The attacker must fund many deposits and operating accounts, and can lose them before earning influence.
